cases.question: Take the forecast run issued at 2026-07-30T18:56:59Z. For Tasmania's half-hour ending at 8:00 am AEST, 31 July 2026, which POE10, POE50 and POE90 operational demand values did it give, and how much operational demand was actually recorded in that half-hour?

how much operational demand was actually recorded
cases.notes: Supply; I agree it is resolved. Region TAS1. The half-hour ending 08:00 AEST on 31 July 2026 is (07:30, 08:00] Hobart time (AEST in July), i.e. 2026-07-30T21:30Z to 22:00Z. One run is named by its exact issue time (2026-07-30T18:56:59Z = 04:56:59 AEST, before the half-hour), so the run selection is issued_at. It asks for that run's POE10/50/90 values and the actual operational demand for the same half-hour, with no error figure: a single-interval comparison. No cutoff. The half-hour lies in the TAS1 31 July event window but is the one after the event's peak half-hour (ending 07:30 AEST), so the scope is a plain half-hour, not event_peak_half_hour.

cases.question: As of 2026-08-19T20:00:00Z, looking only at runs already public, what was the newest Victorian operational demand forecast for the 23:00 to 23:30 UTC half-hour, at POE10, POE50 and POE90?

cases.notes: Supply; I agree it is resolved, with one caveat. Region VIC1. 'As of 2026-08-19T20:00:00Z, looking only at runs already public ... the newest' is an as-of cutoff with as_of_availability: the newest run public by 2026-08-19T20:00Z. The target is 'the 23:00 to 23:30 UTC half-hour', which states no date of its own; I read it on the question's only date, 2026-08-19 (UTC), i.e. 2026-08-19T23:00Z to 23:30Z (09:00 to 09:30 AEST on 20 August), three hours after the cutoff. That is the only natural reading (the next day is outside the data and the previous day would precede the cutoff), but the date comes from the cutoff's timestamp rather than being stated for the half-hour, so a strict reader might want it confirmed. Asking for the POE10/50/90 values without actuals is a forecast value. The half-hour coincides with the VIC1 20 August event's peak half-hour, but the question does not refer to the event, so I label it half_hour only.

cases.question: As of 2026-07-30T14:35:00Z, what did the latest issued forecast say for the SA1 peak half-hour on 2026-07-31?
cases.notes: Ambiguity; outcome clarify_which_forecast, with the owner's two pre-registered outcomes listed. 'The latest issued forecast' does not show what was forecast. For 'the SA1 peak half-hour' on a high-price event date, a predispatch price forecast is at least as natural as a demand forecast, and a weather forecast is possible. My own judgement: CAPABILITIES.md says a forecast whose kind is not shown is not assumed to be demand, so I would not accept the demand reading ('resolved') myself; I list it only because the owner pre-registered it. Under CAPABILITIES.md, event_review_unclear would also be acceptable. The demand-reading fields as I read the question: region SA1; 'the SA1 peak half-hour on 2026-07-31' is the peak half-hour of the SA1 31 July high-price event (peak five-minute interval ending 02:05 ACST on 31 July, 02:35 market time), i.e. (16:30, 17:00]Z on 30 July = 02:00 to 02:30 ACST on 31 July; the date is read as the local (and market) date, since in UTC the peak falls on 30 July. 'Peak' could also mean the day's demand peak, but the only supported scope it can name is the event's peak half-hour. 'What did ... say' is a forecast value. 'As of 2026-07-30T14:35:00Z ... the latest issued' is as_of_availability with cutoff 2026-07-30T14:35Z (00:05 ACST on 31 July, before the target); a reader might take 'latest issued' by issue time rather than by public availability, but an as-of cutoff limits what was public. Tool eligibility is given for the demand reading (eligible); under the clarify outcome, demand forecast tools would not be used. The domain field holds my own reading (unclear), not the demand reading.

cases.question: Based only on data published by noon Brisbane time on Sunday 5 October 2025, what was the highest operational demand in Queensland over that entire local day, and at what time?
request_anchors: the highest operational demand in Queensland
cases.notes: Supply; I agree it is resolved, as a demand-maximum request, not a forecast request. It asks when and at what level actual operational demand in QLD1 was highest over the whole local day of Sunday 5 October 2025 (Brisbane, AEST, no daylight saving): 2025-10-04T14:00Z to 2025-10-05T14:00Z. The request field as_of_utc 2025-10-05T02:00:00Z is authoritative and agrees with 'published by noon Brisbane time' (12:00 AEST = 02:00Z). The cutoff limits what data was public; it does not shorten the window, so the window stays the whole day even though the afternoon was not yet published at the cutoff. No forecast is asked about, so demand forecast tools are not_restricted, and operation, scope and run are null. Intents: CAPABILITIES.md lists demand maxima as its own capability without tying it to one investigation; either investigation that reads actual demand could serve it, although with no price event that day the forecast-review route is the more natural.
